ManagedAgentBacking.description:
What backs the runtime Bridge would launch.

Separate from lifecycle state because the two are independent: an agent can be `ready` backed by a managed payload or by the user's own copy, and only the first is Bridge's to remove.

oneOf.description: A user-managed runtime Bridge can see but must never remove.
A path the user configured explicitly.
A copy shipped inside the app bundle.

ManagedAgentFailure.description: A bounded, redacted record of the last failure.

context.description: Already redacted and length-bounded by the lifecycle layer.

ManagedAgentReceiptSummary.description:
What a receipt says, reduced to what a client can display.

Deliberately omits `ownedPaths` and `entrypoint`: those authorize deletion, and a UI has no use for them. Absent entirely for a runtime Bridge does not own.

source.description: Where the installed bytes came from.

executable.description: The executable that would actually launch, when one resolves. Absent when nothing does.

processId.description: Process id when one is running.

removable.description: True when Bridge holds a receipt for this agent's payload, so removing it is Bridge's to do. True for a payload that drifted as well: Bridge still owns those bytes and can still remove them, which is why this is not the same question as "is it healthy".

state.description: The lifecycle state's stable wire string.

vendorMessage.description: A vendor-owned message, such as a login requirement, carried verbatim. Never a Bridge failure and never credential state.

version.description: The version of the copy that would actually launch, when known.

description: A managed payload and a detected external runtime, reported separately so a caller can always tell which one it is looking at.

externalRuntime.description: A user-managed runtime, if one was detected. Reported so it is visible, never so it can be removed.

receipt.description: Present only when Bridge owns a payload.
